answer: In this PoA design, identity verification uses a Wesolowski VDF: a prescribed chain of modular squarings is sequential because each square depends on the preceding value, and the final result carries a succinct proof. Simulating many identities cannot collapse these chains into one GPU-parallel computation; extra hardware may run instances separately, but every clone retains its own latency, creating a strict physical time bottleneck across canyon, basalt, and wharf.
